job.title: Manager, Corporate Development
job.description:
About the Role 

We’re partnering with a global business services provider backed by one of the world’s leading private markets investors, on a key Corporate Development Manager hire in Singapore.

This is a rare opportunity to join a lean, high-calibre deal team and play a meaningful role in shaping the company’s growth strategy — with exposure to transactions across APAC, the US and LATAM.


Key Responsibilities

  • Support the full M&A lifecycle, from target identification and preliminary assessment through valuation, due diligence, negotiation and closing
  • Build and maintain financial and M&A models, including forecasting, scenario and sensitivity analysis
  • Conduct financial analysis, valuation and comparable transaction analysis
  • Coordinate and manage financial and commercial due diligence workstreams, working with multiple internal and external stakeholders
  • Evaluate transaction feasibility, revenue and cost synergies
  • Prepare investment papers and materials for senior management and investment committee review
  • Work closely with Commercial, Finance, Legal, Tax, HR, IT and external advisers throughout the transaction process
  • Support integration and separation planning where required


Desired Requirements

  • 5–7 years of relevant experience in Corporate Development, M&A, Corporate Finance, Transaction Services / FDD or Investment Banking
  • Hands-on experience across M&A transactions, financial due diligence, valuation and financial modelling
  • Proven ability to manage transaction processes, projects and multiple stakeholders
  • Strong business acumen, commercial judgement and analytical rigour
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Cross-border / multi-jurisdictional transaction experience is preferred
  • Experience in professional services, fund services or business services is advantageous
  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics or a related discipline; CPA, ACCA, CFA or equivalent qualification is a plus


Why Join?

  • End-to-end M&A exposure — be involved from sourcing through closing, rather than operating within a single transaction workstream
  • Join a highly experienced deal team with significant autonomy and responsibility
  • Gain exposure to international transactions across APAC, US and LATAM
  • Work within a PE-backed environment 
  • Take on a role with real visibility and impact on the organisation’s growth strategy
  • Opportunity to broaden your experience across different transactions, markets and business sectors


If you’re an M&A professional looking to move into a high-ownership, principal-side role with genuine end-to-end transaction exposure, feel free to reach out for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Assistant Manager

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage an assigned portfolio of Singapore and offshore entities, including VCCs
  • Act as a trusted corporate secretarial adviser and key client contact
  • Independently handle complex corporate secretarial matters, incorporations, restructurings and statutory filings
  • Advise clients on Singapore Companies Act and ACRA requirements
  • Manage onboarding, KYC and compliance documentation
  • Review and allocate work across the team, while mentoring and supporting junior colleagues

You’ll join a global platform with significant regional and international growth ambitions, while working within a lean Singapore team where your technical expertise and client relationships will have genuine visibility.

It’s a good fit for a strong Senior Executive / Assistant Manager who is ready to take broader ownership, rather than moving into a purely administrative management role.

job.title: Company Secretary
job.description:
About the Opportunity

An established international corporate and fiduciary services group is investing in senior corporate secretarial coverage in its boutique Singapore office, and the client base here is growing.

This is a rare seat with real ownership. You would act as company secretary for a portfolio of client companies. You would set up the entity database, the compliance calendar and the procedures, and shape how the desk runs as the office grows. It comes with direct access to the Managing Director, not a maintenance seat inside an established department.

The Role

You would own the corporate secretarial function end to end for a portfolio of Singapore private limited companies — roughly the scale a busy corporate services desk carries.

Day to day that means:

  • Acting as company secretary for a portfolio of client companies
  • Owning the full statutory cycle for private limited companies — AGMs, annual returns, XBRL filings, dividend distributions, and share issuances and transfers
  • Maintaining registers, drafting directors' and members' resolutions, and keeping every entity in good standing with ACRA
  • Managing the seasonal, filing-driven rhythm across the portfolio so nothing slips
  • Building the function's infrastructure — the entity database, the compliance calendar and the procedures — with a real say in the corporate secretarial software the firm invests in
  • Working directly with the Managing Director and alongside a small, collegiate client-facing and accounting team

What Makes You a Fit

  • You are a Qualified Individual (QI). This is essential for the role.
  • You can act as company secretary for a portfolio of client companies.
  • You have solid Singapore private-company corporate secretarial experience — AGMs, annual returns, XBRL filings, dividends, and share issuances and transfers.
  • You are at manager level and hands-on.

Helpful but not essential: experience setting up a corporate secretarial function from scratch, exposure to corporate secretarial software, and comfort working with an international client base.

One thing worth being straight about: this is a boutique, entrepreneurial environment, not a large corporate with a fixed promotion ladder. The growth here is real — you can build and eventually lead your own team as the business scales — but it comes from building something, not from a two-year title cycle. The people who thrive here are drawn to exactly that.
 

What is On Offer

  • A competitive package with a discretionary bonus, generous leave, medical coverage, a gym benefit and sponsorship for relevant courses
  • Real ownership — you build and shape the cosec desk rather than inherit someone else's
  • Direct access to the Managing Director and real influence over how the function runs
  • A growing, international client base and the runway to build your own team over time
  • Singapore-based, four days in the office with one day from home after probation

job.title: Legal Counsel - Infrastructure Investments (Confidential)
job.description:
About the Opportunity

A Singapore-based alternative investment manager is adding a lawyer to its in-house legal function. This is a newly created position within an established business that invests across Asia.

The organisation manages institutional capital and invests in infrastructure-related businesses and assets. Its strategy combines investment activity with the ongoing development of portfolio companies, giving the legal function exposure to matters that continue beyond the initial acquisition.

The position is being added as the investment programme and portfolio develop. The work is therefore expected to cover more than isolated transaction review, following relevant matters from capital formation and investment through ownership and portfolio development. 

Reporting line remains flexible and will be determined according to the experience of the person appointed. The scope may also be calibrated around the successful candidate, with M&A capability as the common requirement.
 

The Role

This is a broad in-house investment role with expected exposure to both fund-related matters and transaction work. The final allocation between these areas remains to be confirmed.
 

Fund and Capital Matters

  • Support fund formation and ongoing fund documentation, potentially including LPAs, side letters and related investor documentation. 
  • Assist with co-investment and other capital arrangements connected to investment activity. 
  • Work with relevant internal functions where legal matters touch fundraising, investor commitments, governance or fund operations. 
 

Investments and Transactions

  • Take a central legal role in M&A activity involving infrastructure-related businesses and assets. Strong M&A is the confirmed core requirement.
  • Support transactions from structuring and due diligence through documentation, negotiation and completion. 
  • Advise on joint ventures, corporate structuring, follow-on acquisitions and transaction-related financing where relevant. 
  • Coordinate external counsel across relevant jurisdictions while keeping legal work aligned with the commercial objective of each transaction.  
 

Portfolio Development

  • Work with investment and asset-management colleagues after acquisition as portfolio businesses grow, undertake further transactions or enter new markets. 
  • Support legal matters arising from additional capital deployment, strategic partnerships, development activity and portfolio-level M&A. 
  • Help translate transaction terms into workable governance and ownership arrangements.

job.title: VP Investor Relations
job.description:
About the Opportunity

An Asia-based infrastructure investment firm is adding an investor relations professional to its fundraising team.

The firm is in market, and the fundraising calendar here does not stop when a close lands. Separately managed accounts and co-investment work run alongside the primary raise, so LP meetings, calls and information requests are continuous rather than cyclical. This is a new seat rather than a replacement, added as that activity builds.

You would report to the managing director who leads the function regionally.
 

The Role

Two things sit at the centre of this seat.

The first is the calendar. A high volume of LP meetings and calls, and all of the logistics behind them, run through this person.

The second is acting as deal captain on due diligence questionnaires and LP information requests. You would not be expected to answer every question yourself. You would own the process: routing questions to the right people across investments, finance and asset management, holding the deadline, and making sure what goes back to the LP is accurate and consistent with what has gone before.

This is an internal-facing seat by design. You would not carry LP accounts or pitch independently. Client-facing exposure comes through shadowing the managing director at LP meetings and industry events, which is how this person is expected to build LP fluency over time.
 

What Makes You a Fit

  • Five to ten years in fundraising or investor relations, with at least five of those years LP-facing. The split matters more than the total. 
  • Infrastructure background in a must
  • You can speak credibly about who the major LPs in this space are, and how a standard DDQ and reporting cycle actually runs.
  • English is required. Additional languages are useful rather than necessary.
  • Commitment, determination and integrity count for more here than polish.

job.title: Human Resources Specialist
job.description:

What You'll Be Doing

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Managing cross-border HR operations across the employee lifecycle, including employment contracts, onboarding, offboarding, payroll, benefits, immigration, employment tax and social security administration.
  • Supporting the setup and implementation of HR operations in new markets, including local employment contracts, HR policies and benefits frameworks.

What We're Looking For

Why Consider This Opportunity?

If you're looking to accelerate your HR career within a high-performing international environment, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Head of Accounting Services
job.description:
About the Opportunity

An established international professional and corporate services firm is hiring a Head of Accounting Services to lead its accounting business across ASEAN, spanning Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia. This is a genuine regional leadership seat: ownership of the accounting service line and its commercial performance across the three markets, a mandate to set accounting strategy and quality standards, and a platform built to scale. You would report into senior regional management and be based in Kuala Lumpur, with some flexibility on base location for the right person..

This is not a caretaker role. The firm has been growing across the region and wants a commercially-minded, client-facing leader who can front CFO and finance-director conversations, back up business development, and lift the teams from routine bookkeeping toward larger, more complex engagements — while keeping local teams close to their clients and regulators. Depth of seniority matters less than commercial ability and client-facing credibility — this is a platform where a capable leader can step up into a broader remit, so we are open to a range of backgrounds rather than one narrow profile.


The Role

You would own the Accounting Services line across the three markets, end to end:

  • Carry commercial accountability for the service line — revenue, margin, utilisation, work-in-progress, pricing and resourcing across Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia.
  • Lead and develop the senior managers who run local delivery, setting clear regional priorities, business plans and performance expectations.
  • Own the most senior and complex client relationships, act as the regional escalation point, and move clients from transactional accounting toward higher-value reporting and advisory work.
  • Set a consistent regional operating model: common methodologies, quality standards, review processes and service-delivery expectations, while respecting jurisdiction-specific requirements.
  • Drive the technology and transformation agenda — cloud accounting platforms, automation and standardised workflows.
  • Contribute to business development and cross-border client opportunities as the platform grows.

Think regional architect and hands-on technical authority in one seat: close enough to the accounting to be credible with your teams and clients, senior enough to run the numbers and the strategy.


What Makes You a Fit

First and foremost, you are commercially minded and client-facing. You are comfortable in front of CFOs, finance directors and boards — pitching the outsourcing of a finance function, defending a service scope, and translating a client conversation into what your teams can deliver. You are business-minded rather than a pure technician, and you enjoy backing up sales to help win new work. Just as important is how you work with people: you build easy, credible relationships with senior clients and with peers across a regional leadership team.

On the technical side, a solid accounting grounding is expected rather than exceptional — a Big Four or mid-tier-firm background, comfort with IFRS and local reporting, and the ability to guide your teams on complex matters when it counts. Depth of seniority is not the point — what counts is that you have led or supported larger, more complex engagements and are ready to carry commercial responsibility, so you do not need a long title or a big portfolio behind you. You have ideally led or helped lead delivery across more than one office or market, or you are ready to take on that regional oversight, with a strong home-market (Malaysia ideally) statutory base and a working understanding of the Singapore and Indonesia environments.

Ideally you have carried some service-line commercial responsibility — a revenue-to-gross-profit view, or the pricing, utilisation and margin behind the work — and you are comfortable inheriting and growing client relationships with a genuine nose for business development.

You hold a degree in Accounting or Finance, you are based in Malaysia with the right to work there (a Malaysian citizen, or already holding a Malaysian work visa), and your business English is strong.

Helpful, though not essential: a professional qualification such as ACCA, CPA, ICAEW, CIMA or MICPA and MIA membership; a background in corporate services, fund services or professional-services outsourcing (though we are keen to look more broadly); experience standardising or bringing teams onto a common operating model; exposure to accounting technology and transformation; and basic Mandarin.

 

What is On Offer

  • A genuine regional remit across three markets — Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia — rather than a narrow single-country brief, owning the accounting service line and its commercial performance from revenue to gross profit.
  • The opportunity to build, standardise and scale a regional accounting platform and to shape its quality and technology agenda.
  • A seat in the core ASEAN management team with genuine visibility across the regional business, and real potential for the remit to broaden as the platform scales.

job.title: Strategic Finance Associate
job.description:
About the opportunity


A well-capitalised, asset-heavy real estate platform backed by institutional private equity is building out its strategic finance capability across its Asia Pacific markets. This is a Singapore-based seat created to bring genuine forward-looking finance into a business that has grown quickly and now wants sharper decision support behind the numbers. You would join a small, high-calibre strategic finance team that sits close to pricing and data analytics, in a data-driven operating rhythm, with direct and regular exposure to senior leadership.


The role

This is not a month-end-and-variance seat. You would own the monthly P&L across multiple markets, consolidate it, and turn it into the one insight leadership actually needs — the kind of read that spots a revenue dip in one market, traces it to the real driver, and starts the right cross-functional conversation. You would sit at the centre of the monthly business review as a genuine thought partner, and you would rebuild the budgeting and forecasting model from something basic into something that holds up across markets and feeds straight into the operating rhythm and KPI tracking.

In short, you turn the numbers into decisions, and you build the machinery that keeps doing it.
 

What makes you a fit

You have likely spent 4 to 7 years in strategic or corporate finance, or in a forward-looking FP&A or commercial finance seat where you owned the model rather than just maintained it. You are strong on driver-based modelling and scenario analysis, and you are comfortable building from a blank sheet. You can read a P&L commercially, connect it to what is happening in the business, and hold your own in a room with senior leaders — voicing a view, defending it with analysis, and being challenged on it without flinching.

Just as important, you carry real technical finance rigour. You can speak to consolidation, controls, and the quality of the numbers, because this seat is scrutinised by senior finance as much as by the commercial side.

If you come from a Big Four background, you are welcome here provided you have already made the move in-house and are past the early adjustment out of audit. Real estate or other asset-heavy, capex-heavy exposure is a plus rather than a must. Data fluency — SQL, Python, or BI tools — is a bonus that will serve you well in this environment.

One thing worth being honest about: the right person is moving for the next challenge, not the next pay band. This is a seat for someone ambitious and self-driven who still wants to be stretched, and who is humble enough to be challenged and to collaborate with an existing team.


What is on offer

A competitive base with a performance-based bonus, and something rarer than comp — a near-greenfield mandate to shape how a multi-market business plans, measures, and decides. You get genuine ownership, a direct line to senior leadership, and regional scope from day one. For the right person, this is a platform to become the finance partner the business cannot run its review without.


Open to interim or contract, too

Alongside the permanent search, the business is also open to an experienced candidate on a short-term contract basis (around 3 to 6 months) to support the function through a transition.

This track is strictly for someone who can be hands-on from day one — no ramp-up, no hand-holding. To be clear about what that requires:

  • Senior enough to walk in and run the monthly multi-market P&L consolidation and the modelling independently, from week one.
  • A real estate or asset-heavy finance background is required for this track (not just a plus), so the operating context is already familiar.
  • Available now or on very short notice to bridge cleanly.

If you would need time to get up to speed, this interim track is not the right fit — though the permanent role above may still be. For the right person there may be scope for the contract to extend or convert.

job.title: Head of Fund Services
job.description:
About the Opportunity

A well-established global fund administration and corporate services group is building out the senior leadership of its Hong Kong fund services business. This is a newly created Head of Funds seat, not a backfill, created to bring sharper strategic leadership, stronger operations, and a steady senior hand to a respected, client-focused team. You would lead both the funds and investor services functions, report into regional operations leadership, and have genuine scope to shape how the Hong Kong business runs.


The Role

This is a build-and-improve mandate. In your first year you will get close to the work, including reviews and month-end and the realities of day-to-day delivery, so that you understand where the team is strong and where it is not. From there the focus shifts to the strategic: streamlining how work flows, lifting operational standards, and partnering with the wider service network of the group to run a more efficient Hong Kong team. You will own and deepen key client relationships, and you will work alongside business development on pitches, bringing operational realism to what gets committed to clients. Expect to mentor experienced people, balance competing priorities across two teams, and be the senior operator that clients and colleagues turn to.

What Makes You a Fit

You have built a strong fund accounting foundation inside a fund administrator or on the buy-side, and you are genuinely comfortable across the fund lifecycle, including NAV, financial statements and capital calls, rather than only at the oversight layer. You are clearly senior: someone who has led teams, settled in above experienced colleagues, and earned credibility quickly. You think in terms of process and efficiency, ideally with exposure to offshore or shared-service delivery, and you can tell the difference between what should stay close to the client and what should not. You are commercially aware but operationally honest, able to manage expectations and push back when something cannot be delivered well. Chinese language, Cantonese and/or Mandarin, and a Hong Kong or China background with overseas exposure will set you apart. Experience spanning private equity, private credit, real estate or hedge structures is welcome.


What is On Offer

A competitive base for the platform, with room to flex for the right person, plus the benefits you would expect from an established global group. More than that, this is a rare and genuinely senior seat where you are not one of many: you would shape the Hong Kong business directly, with clear progression potential into broader leadership over time, backed by a group with an established international service network.

job.title: Associate Vice President - Real Estate Fund Accounting
job.description:
AVP – Real Estate Fund Administration

Fund Administration | Real Assets / Alternative Investments | Singapore
Confidential Search

The Opportunity

We are representing a global fund services platform supporting clients across alternative investments and real assets. As part of continued business growth, the firm is seeking an AVP – Real Estate Fund Administration to support a portfolio of real estate investment structures and oversee day-to-day fund administration activities.

This role combines fund accounting oversight, client servicing, stakeholder coordination, and team supervision within a regulated financial services environment.

The successful candidate will work closely with senior management while supervising a small team and acting as a key contact point for clients, investors, auditors, and other fund stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Fund Administration & Accounting Oversight

  • Support the administration of a portfolio of real estate and alternative investment funds in accordance with administration agreements and operational requirements
  • Maintain oversight of books and records, including review of Net Asset Value (NAV) calculations
  • Coordinate and review financial statements, periodic reports, and related performance reporting
  • Coordinate and review investor allocations relating to capital calls and distributions
  • Review capital account statements and related investor reporting documentation
  • Support payment processing activities and operational transaction flows

Client & Stakeholder Management

  • Act as a primary day-to-day contact point for assigned clients and fund participants
  • Maintain professional relationships with investors, investment managers, banks, auditors, and other stakeholders
  • Work closely with Investor Relations teams to support investor communications and capital activity notices
  • Assist with client queries, service matters, and ongoing operational coordination

Team Leadership & Operational Support

  • Supervise and review work performed by junior team members
  • Provide guidance and support to team members on operational and reporting matters
  • Monitor deliverables to ensure service quality and compliance with agreed timelines
  • Assist with issue escalation and operational problem resolution where required

Projects & Process Improvement

  • Participate in internal projects and initiatives supporting operational improvement and business growth
  • Support presentations and discussions with existing or prospective clients where required
  • Monitor compliance with service agreements and operational procedures
  • Contribute to process enhancement initiatives across the business

Requirements

Experience

  • Minimum 4 years of experience within fund administration, accounting, asset management, or financial services environments
  • Prior exposure to real estate, real assets, or alternative investment fund structures
  • Experience supervising or guiding junior team members within a team environment

Education & Qualifications

  • Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related discipline
  • Professional accounting qualification (e.g. CA, CPA, ACCA, or equivalent) completed or in progress would be advantageous

Technical Skills

  • Experience reviewing general ledgers and financial statements
  • Familiarity with consolidation concepts and financial reporting processes
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint

Skills & Competencies

An established Singapore-based private equity firm is hiring an Executive Assistant to support select members of its investment team. This is a team EA seat — not a single-principal household PA role — and sits alongside the wider EA bench in a collegial, cover-each-other model.

You will provide secretariat support to select members of the investment team, alongside shared office operations and basic IT administration. The remit splits across three areas.

Executive support to the investment team

You have spent at least five years in a true Executive Assistant capacity, ideally as a team EA supporting more than one executive in a fast-paced environment — private equity, asset management, family office, hedge fund, or boutique investment bank is a strong plus. You are technologically comfortable. You can troubleshoot the everyday issues that come up in a modern office, you pick up new tools quickly, and you are happy to be the go-to person for the team on anything from a stuck printer to a calendar sync issue.

This is a Singapore-based, hybrid Business Development Director seat with a global investor services and fund administration firm with a long-established presence across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The APAC business is a meaningful engine for the wider group — the platform sells the full shelf: fund administration, corporate services, fiduciary, depositary, and regulatory solutions across PE, hedge, real assets, and credit strategies.

The seat reports directly into the Regional Chief Commercial Officer for APAC. You land into an established sales function with delivery and servicing teams already in place across Singapore and Hong Kong, and a mandate to drive new-logo growth in the Singapore market and across the wider region.
 

The Role

This is a hunter mandate. Day one looks like territory mapping, prospect lists, and getting the calendar full of business partner meetings — not waiting for marketing leads.

You will:

  • Own a defined APAC territory and a personal new-business pipeline across PE GPs, hedge fund managers, closed and open-ended fund managers, and selected corporate clients.
  • Run prospecting end-to-end — outbound, referral, market intelligence, and conference work — and translate that into qualified pipeline.

  • Maintain a steady cadence of business partner meetings and prospect wins each month, with a clear ramp expectation in the first six months and a step up thereafter.

  • Represent the firm at industry events and stay close to regulatory and structuring trends across Singapore, Hong Kong, and offshore (Cayman, BVI).

The seat is sized for someone who has carried a number, not someone who has supported a process. If you are most proud of the pipeline you have personally built and the new logos you have personally landed, this seat is built around that profile.
 

What Makes You a Fit

You have probably spent 8 or more years in client-facing business development inside a fund administrator, asset servicer, or directly adjacent financial services platform — the kind of seat where a quarterly pipeline review is a real conversation, not a slide.

You have carried a quota, won new logos, and can talk through your last few wins with deal size, timeframe, and how the deal actually came together. You sell across PE, hedge, and closed/open-ended fund managers — and you are equally comfortable on a discovery call with a CFO at a mid-market PE shop and on a panel of stakeholders at a multi-strategy hedge fund.

You bring an active, warm APAC network — not "I know the market", but specific names you would call in week one. You have owned an RFP end-to-end, not just supported the bid team, and you can describe how you sequence Operations, Tax, and Legal inputs to hit a deadline.

The strongest fits will also bring some combination of:

  • Existing relationships with PE GPs, fund-of-funds, and family offices in the region.
  • Hedge and closed-end product fluency alongside private equity.
  • A track record of multi-year strategic accounts, not just one-shot wins.
  • Demonstrable RFP authoring and proposal-writing chops alongside the oral selling.
 

What is On Offer

  • A competitive base salary positioned at the senior end of the Singapore BDD market, plus an annual commission plan with meaningful new-logo and RFP-win economics on top.
  • A direct reporting line into the Regional Chief Commercial Officer, APAC — quick decisions, visible mandate, no layers between you and the people who set the strategy.

  • A hybrid working pattern out of a CBD office.
